shots.say: Look! Two ears in the grass, and they're turning different ways! Who is it?
shots.tag: hook: two ears in the grass

shots.say: Three animals are hiding! We can only see their ears.
I'm Milo the bluebird. Let's play Guess With Milo!
The Animated Zoo!
Look closely at the ears, and say your guess. Ready? Let's play!
Here are two ears. They are gray, with a little fringe of hair. Whose ears are they?
Is it the rhino? Or is it the zebra?
It is the rhino!
Here is the fun fact. A rhino can move each ear, on its own!
One ear can point forward, while the other ear points back!
Watch the ears! Forward, and back. Forward, and back!
What does a rhino do, when it hears something interesting?
Both ears perk straight up! Boing!
Up go the ears, to listen very closely. Perk!
Now point both hands straight up, like perky rhino ears. Perk!
A rhino can't see very well. But it hears very well!
Point one hand forward, and one hand back, like rhino ears!
Say it with me. A rhino can move each ear, on its own!
Now be very quiet, like a listening rhino. What can you hear?
Quick check! Can a rhino turn its two ears different ways? Yes, or no?
Yes! One ear forward, one ear back. Great job!
Here are two more ears. Look! They are so big, and pointy! Whose ears are they?
Is it the fox? Or is it the rabbit?
It is the fennec fox!
Here is the fun fact. A fennec fox is a little fox, with giant ears!
Its ears can be half as long as its body!
shots.tag: half as long as its body

shots.say: Wow! That is a lot of ear, for a little fox!
Count the giant ears with me. One, two!
What do those giant ears do?
They listen for food, hiding under the sand. Like a little beetle!
Then the fox digs with all four feet. Dig, dig, dig!
And big ears let extra heat out. That helps the fox stay cool, in the hot desert!
Cup your hands behind your ears, like big fox ears. Listen!
Say it with me. A fennec fox has giant ears!
Can you dig like a fennec fox? Dig, dig, dig!
Quick check! What do the fox's big ears listen for? Food under the sand, or a drum?
Food under the sand! Super listening!
Here are the last ears. They are small, and round. Whose ears are they?
Is it the polar bear? Or is it the fennec fox?
It is the polar bear!
Here is the fun fact. A polar bear has small, round ears!
Count the little ears with me. One, two!
Why are a polar bear's ears so small?
Small ears help keep the warmth in, in the cold, snowy Arctic!
Big fox ears let heat out. Small bear ears keep the warmth in!
And look! A polar bear has a short little tail. It keeps the warmth in, too!
Can you shiver, like you are in the snow? Brrr!
Make small ears! Cover your ears with your hands. So cozy!
Say it with me. A polar bear has small, round ears!
Can you hug yourself, warm and cozy, like a polar bear? Squeeze!
Quick check! Which ears keep the warmth in? Big ears, or small ears?
Small ears! You remembered!
Three pairs of ears, and three friends! Now it is quiz time!
Whose ears can turn different ways? The rhino's, or the polar bear's?
The rhino! One ear forward, one ear back.
Whose giant ears listen under the sand? The fox's, or the rhino's?
The fennec fox! Listen, listen!
Whose ears are small and round? The fox's, or the polar bear's?
The polar bear! Small ears keep it warm.
Look at all our ear friends! You guessed them all!
Turn your ears like a rhino. Cup your ears like a fox. And cover them, so cozy, like a polar bear!
Next time on Guess With Milo: whose egg is this? Bye-bye, friends!
The Animated Zoo!
